mode_evidence: Thomas and Lang classify crystal pictures as 'pseudo-hallucinations, or objects apparently external but not forming in any real sense part of the outside world', analogous to hypnagogic imagery but seen wide awake. Lang compares them to a speck of colour before shut eyes developing into a face. One account has a dark funnel 'filled with light', i.e. light seen in a dark space without a source. The source itself leaves open whether it is perceptual or imaginal.
onset_evidence: Lang: go alone, back to the light, ball on a dark cloth, exclude reflections, stare about five minutes; if nothing in two or three trials, probably never. Thomas disagrees: Indian Mussulman practice recommends three quarters of an hour or more, and two or three trials are too few. Strong visualisers often fail while others succeed; the faculty can be absent for weeks. Also an account of a first success by looking into a perfectly dark funnel with the head covered, which filled with light before pictures.

what_to_do_with_light: Keep gazing; the mist may vanish leaving only the pictures. Record at once.
obstacles_and_fixes: Nothing in a few trials: Lang says give up, Thomas says continue far longer
Power absent for weeks even in a gifted scryer
Reflections and points de repere: exclude them if one wants to exclude artefact
cautions: Moderate indulgence is no more harmful than an after-dinner snooze (Thomas)
Historical Church condemnations of scrying as heresy are quoted
interpretation: A day-dream-like pseudo-hallucination, allied to visualising, analogous to hypnagogic imagery but occurring in wide-awake people; veridical cases are discussed as telepathy.
practice_summary: Go alone into a room, sit with your back to the light, and set the glass ball in your lap on a dark cloth so no reflections reach it. Stare at it for about five minutes, thinking of anything you please. Lang says that if two or three trials show nothing you will probably never succeed; Thomas thinks that far too short and cites Islamic instructions to go on for three quarters of an hour or more, noting the power may vanish for weeks. The usual sequence is that the ball grows milky or misty, may go black, and then pictures appear; some strong visualisers get only the mist. An alternative first trial is to look into a perfectly dark funnel with the head covered, which filled with light before images appeared.
